newsitem.title: GERMANY: UAL's ex-Germany cargo volumes fall 33.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: UAL's ex-Germany cargo volumes fall 33.5 pct.

text.p: United Airlines said its air cargo volumes out of Germany have fallen 33.5 percent percent this year due to a stagnating market and airline over-capacity.
Robert Blythe, the airline's cargo sales manager Germany, told Reuters in an interview United is exporting some 300 tonnes a month of exports this year, compared to about 450 tonnes a month in 1995.
"We are down this year. There is over-capacity on the market and little extra tonnage," he said.
United has at present an average load factor in the high 70s on its daily ex-Frankfurt flights to Chicago and Washington and ex-Duesseldorf to Chicago, he said.
The two Frankfurt routes have been flown with Boeing 777 aircraft since September 9. A Boeing 747 was used on the route for the peak passenger summer months, he noted.
The Duesseldorf route, which started in June, operates with a B767-300, he added.
The bulk of cargo for all three ex-Germany services is generated in Frankfurt, Blythe added.
